prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: In frames 1 and 2, the depth map places a person in a beanie in the lower-right foreground at roughly 1 to 1.5 metres (within arm's reach of the camera wearer and the adjacent table), facing slightly right and downward away from the camera, while a white chair back (~1.2 m) sits to the lower left and a potted plant (~2 to 2.5 m) stands behind and between them (~1 m behind the person) in front of a curtained window and wall shelf (~2.5 m). Across frames 3 to 5, the camera wearer turns rapidly leftward and tilts upward toward an arched doorway (~3 m away) opening into an adjacent living room (~4 to 6 m deep), causing the foreground person, table, and plant to exit the right and bottom edges of the view. The depth map clarifies the continuous 3D geometry of the archway, ceiling plane, and recessed room recess behind the foreground furniture in frames 1, 2, 4, and 5 better than the dark or high-contrast areas of the RGB image. However, the map is unreliable in frame 3 where motion blur flattens the scene into indistinct grey gradients, in frame 4 where the glowing ceiling light fixture (~1.5 to 2 m overhead) is misestimated as extremely close (pure white), and through the window pane in frames 1 and 2 where glass transparency produces a dark depth hole.
descriptions.segmentation: In frames 1 and 2, the segmentation map identifies the person in the lower-right foreground (~1 to 1.5 m away, cropped below the chest and facing downward/right away from the camera wearer), a potted plant (~2 to 2.5 m away to the left and behind the person) resting on a tall vase/pot (~0.5 m below the foliage), several chairs (~1.2 to 2.2 m away on the lower left, behind the person, and at the bottom right within the person's arm's reach), and small bottles on the upper-right wall shelf (~2.5 m away, ~1 m above the person's head). It explicitly separates overlapping object boundaries that blend into the dim RGB background, such as the chair partially occluded behind the person's torso and the plant's upper foliage vs. its lower pot/stand. From frame 1 to frame 2, as the person leans slightly forward and right while the camera shifts slightly upward and left, the masks track the person's silhouette and the white foreground chair shifting toward the lower edge. However, the segmentation map is completely unreliable in frames 3, 4, and 5—producing entirely blank black frames due to severe motion blur in frame 3 and the upward camera rotation toward the ceiling, archway, and distant bookshelves (~4 to 6 m away) in frames 4 and 5—and even in frames 1 and 2 it fragments single chairs into duplicate overlapping 'chair' masks while missing the foreground table, walls, and curtains.
descriptions.pose: In frame 1, the pose map localises the upper-body yellow skeleton and magenta left-hand keypoints of the person ~1 to 1.5 metres away in the lower-right foreground, showing their torso and head angled forward and slightly left while looking downward away from the camera wearer, with both arms bent within arm's reach of their own face (right index finger raised to the nose/glasses, left hand touching the left temple). Because the person's lower body is occluded below the bottom frame edge and by the foreground table, only shoulder, elbow, wrist, and head keypoints are plotted above the waist. This skeletal representation isolates the exact 3D joint articulation of the person's raised arms and compact left-hand finger cluster against their dark black clothing, which strongly camouflages the limbs in the RGB frame. Across frames 2 to 5, as the person leans slightly right and lowers their right hand in frame 2 before sweeping out of view when the camera turns left and upward in frames 3 to 5, the pose map becomes unreliable by failing to detect the person entirely in frame 2 (and the blurred edge of frame 3) despite their upper body remaining clearly visible at ~1 to 1.2 metres in frame 2.
